'''Daniel B. Szyld''' (born 1955 in [[Buenos Aires]]) is an [[Argentines|Argentinian]] and [[Americans|American]] [[mathematician]] who is a professor at [[Temple University]] in Philadelphia. He has made contributions to numerical and applied linear algebra as well as matrix theory.<ref name="amsfellow" /><ref name="siamfelow" />

== Education ==
He was admitted without an undergraduate degree to the graduate school at [[New York University]],<ref name="image61">{{cite magazine|url=https://secureservercdn.net/72.167.241.46/31g.343.myftpupload.com/wp-content/uploads/IMAGE/image61.pdf|magazine=Image: The Bulletin of the International Linear Algebra Society|issue=61|date=Fall 2018|title=The field is continuously evolving in part due to emerging applications|type=Interview with Daniel Szyld|first=Froilán|last=Dopico|pages=6–8}}</ref> where he defended his PhD in 1983.<ref name="mathgenealogy"/> While there, he worked as a research assistant for [[Wassily Leontief]].<ref name="image61"/>

== International awards and appointments ==
He was named as a [[SIAM Fellow]]<ref name="siamfelow">{{Cite web |title=SIAM {{!}} Fellows |url=https://www.siam.org/prizes-recognition/fellows-program/all-siam-fellows/s |access-date=2022-07-14 |website=www.siam.org}}</ref> and as a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]<ref name="amsfellow">{{Cite web |title=Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |url=http://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows.cgi#s |access-date=2022-07-14 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref> in 2017. In 2020, he was elected president of the [[International Linear Algebra Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-12-23 |title=Past ILAS Officers - International Linear Algebra Society |url=https://ilasic.org/past-ilas-officers/ |access-date=2022-07-14 |website=ilasic.org |language=en-US}}</ref> He was [[editor-in-chief]] for the [[Electronic Transactions on Numerical Analysis]] from 2005 to 2013<ref name="etnaeditors">{{Cite web |date=2020-12-23 |title=Numerical Linear Algebra with Applications, Editors |url=https://etna.math.kent.edu/editors/ |access-date=2022-09-15
